prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: ultra-premium 16:9 desktop homepage direction comp for VEEMAP Technologies
Primary request: Design a complete, real, shippable homepage viewport titled "Flowfield Assembly" for an Indian special-purpose machine builder. Use the physical logic of ebru marbling—pigment streamlines displaced by solid bodies—as a bold information system for machine performance. The result must feel exact, technical, and premium, never mystical, decorative, or wellness-oriented.
Input images: Image 1 is the authoritative VEEMAP chevron logo reference—reproduce its orange outer chevron and green inner chevron accurately and tastefully in the header. Images 2 and 3 are visual-quality references only for cream paper, navy/coral pigment language and strong editorial hierarchy; do not copy their logo, brand, wording, exact artwork, or layout.
Scene/backdrop: a polished desktop website screenshot, edge-to-edge 16:9 canvas, no browser chrome. Warm cream technical paper with subtle tooth and an exact navy modular grid. Controlled navy and coral flowfield contours sweep horizontally across the page like CFD streamlines.
Subject: The central hero object is one conceptually accurate, non-proprietary high-speed automated industrial special-purpose assembly machine. It must look mechanically credible: black anodized extrusion frame, brushed stainless guards, transparent safety enclosure, indexing conveyor, servo pick-and-place gantry, robotic end effector, vision camera and compact HMI. Show the exact machine in a controlled exploded configuration: major functional modules are separated by short physically plausible offsets along one common isometric camera axis, with the base coherent. Navy and coral process streamlines bend, accelerate and part around each solid module, then converge into a clean laminar band at the output. This exact machine and camera are designed to later collapse into an assembled scroll keyframe.
Style/medium: precise photoreal 3D industrial product render integrated with editorial printmaking and engineering flow visualization; fine ebru pigment texture is contained inside controlled streamlines and large type, not splashed randomly. High-end engineering studio, sophisticated and unexpected.
Composition/framing: slim top header with VEEMAP logo and wordmark left; navigation "CAPABILITIES", "INDUSTRIES", "ENGINEERING", "CAREERS"; outlined CTA right. Large confident serif headline on the left third, central exploded machine dominating the middle and right. Four circular capability markers sit directly on key machine modules; each connects to a legible small label. A narrow bottom evidence strip and next-section peek make the design obviously buildable as a full website.
Lighting/mood: soft directional studio light, crisp metal and glass, calm technical confidence, high visual contrast.
Color palette: paper cream, deep engineering navy, faded ultramarine, precise coral orange, small authentic VEEMAP green accent, graphite and stainless steel.
Text (verbatim): "VEEMAP TECHNOLOGIES"; "SPECIAL-PURPOSE MACHINE BUILDERS"; "ENGINEER THE FLOW."; "We combine world-class automation assets with in-house R&D to build machines engineered for speed, accuracy and uptime."; "TELL US ABOUT YOUR PROCESS"; "AI VISION"; "HIGH-SPEED MOTION"; "INDUSTRY 4.0 HMI"; "PREDICTIVE HEALTH"; "236 PROJECTS DELIVERED".
Typography: high-contrast editorial serif for the large headline, clean narrow sans-serif for navigation, labels and body copy, disciplined uppercase technical annotations.
Constraints: exact 16:9 wide desktop composition; machine is central, mechanically plausible, and clearly exploded; flowlines visibly react to machine geometry and communicate process throughput; preserve precision and usability; CTA must be visually prominent; only the sourced number 236 may appear; clear web hierarchy; use logo from Image 1 accurately; spelling must be exact.
Avoid: abstract wellness art, meditative language, astrology, ocean/spa motifs, random psychedelic marbling, craft-store aesthetic, fake client logos, fake certifications, invented statistics, proprietary machine detail, brand-name robot components, people, stock factory photos, neon cyberpunk, excessive blur/glow, generic SaaS cards, random pseudo-text, watermarks, browser chrome.
